items.stem: What should come before refactoring untested legacy code?

options.text: Writing characterization tests that capture current behaviour
options.rationale: Correct: a behavioural safety net lets you refactor with confidence.

options.text: Deleting the parts that look unused
options.rationale: Deleting code you do not understand is risky.
Big-bang rewrites discard the safety net and raise risk.
Mass upgrades add risk before you can detect regressions.

items.explanation: Correct: a behavioural safety net lets you refactor with confidence.

items.stem: Which TWO principles make legacy modernization with Cursor safer? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Make small, reversible steps reviewed against tests
options.rationale: Correct: small reversible steps limit and localise risk.

options.text: Understand callers and dependencies before changing code
options.rationale: Correct: knowing the blast radius prevents surprises.

options.text: Replace everything in a single large change
options.rationale: Big-bang changes are hard to review and revert.

options.text: Skip tests because the code is old
options.rationale: Old code needs a safety net more, not less.

items.explanation: Correct: small reversible steps limit and localise risk.

items.stem: Tests still pass after a change, but the suite is thin. What does that tell you?

options.text: Passing thin tests is weak evidence; behaviour may still have changed
options.rationale: Correct: a thin suite cannot prove behaviour was preserved.

options.text: The change is definitely safe to ship
options.rationale: Thin tests do not prove safety.
Passing tests say nothing about coverage completeness.

items.explanation: Correct: a thin suite cannot prove behaviour was preserved.
